event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The 2022 filing makes it unmistakably clear that COVID-19 is not a hypothetical threat but a present-day force already depressing Allegion’s operations and margins.  Multiple passages document realised effects – production slow-downs, plant suspensions, cost inflation, supply-chain choke-points, labour shortages and even management distraction – while simultaneously warning that these pressures will persist and could escalate as new variants appear or vaccine mandates reshape the workforce.  The language is highly specific (naming shortages of electronic components, freight delays, remote-work cyber-risk, etc.) and ties each issue directly to COVID-19.  Although no exact dollar figures or percentage hits are provided, the company repeatedly uses intensifiers such as “significantly delayed,” “material adverse impact,” and “large investment of time and resources,” signalling materiality.  Given the filing date (Feb-2022) is less than three years after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time Decay Principle permits high scores.  Overall, the disclosure depicts an elevated, continuing risk environment with only limited mitigating detail, justifying generally high—but not maximum—severity ratings for the cited evidence.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business operations have been, and are expected to continue to be, adversely impacted by the global COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: States that impacts have already occurred (realised risk).
Explicit expectation of continued adverse impact (forward-looking risk).
Direct causal link to the global COVID-19 pandemic.
No quantitative magnitude disclosed.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly attributes both past and future harm to COVID-19, but lack of quantification tempers score to 6.

evidence_list.snippet: We are unable to predict the full extent to which the pandemic and related impacts, including macroeconomic impacts and the pace of global economic recovery, will continue to adversely impact our business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Admits ongoing adverse impact potential.
Highlights uncertainty and uncontrollability, signalling possible greater severity.
Generic forward-looking disclaimer dilutes precision.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges unknown but continuing downside; generic wording keeps score modest.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and preventative measures taken to contain the spread of COVID-19 or mitigate this pandemic have caused, and are continuing to cause, business slowdowns or shutdowns in various countries around the world.

components.reason: Reports actual slowdowns/shutdowns already experienced.
States impacts are still ongoing.
Global scope (“various countries around the world”).
No specific financial metric.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates worldwide operational disruption that is both historical and current, warranting a high score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: This pandemic has also caused, and may continue to cause, disruption to our global supply chain and business operations, in addition to the various effects noted elsewhere within the risk factors contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

components.reason: Explicitly links supply-chain disruption to COVID-19.
Emphasises future continuation of disruption.
Describes impact as global in scope.
Lacks numeric detail.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct cause-and-effect on supply chain with forward-looking angle earns mid-high score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Numerous actions taken to help limit the spread of COVID-19, such as stay-at-home orders, quarantines, increased border controls and closures, business shutdowns, and other public health and government mandates that restrict business activities and travel have impacted, and will likely continue to impact our ability to carry out business as usual, including the temporary suspension of some of our operations, shortages in materials, parts and components, fluctuations in customer demand, costs associated with operational changes and an extended period of remote work arrangements for some of our employees which could increase cybersecurity risks and other operational risks.

components.reason: Details multiple concrete operational impacts (suspensions, shortages, demand shifts).
States impacts are expected to continue.
Touches on added cyber-risk from remote work, broadening risk categories.
Government mandates indicate external, uncontrollable drivers of risk.
No quantified dollar effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive listing of present and future operational strains produces a strong score despite lack of quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: In particular, shortages in commodities and materials, including shortages and reductions in allocations of electronic and other components from key suppliers, labor shortages and elevated levels of employee absenteeism, freight delays and other supply chain constraints and disruptions have significantly delayed or disrupted, and may continue to adversely impact, both our suppliers’ and our ability to manufacture and deliver products to our customers.

components.reason: Cites ‘significant’ delays/disruptions already realised.
Specifies multiple bottlenecks (components, labor, freight).
Warns of continued adverse impact.
Severity qualifier (‘significantly’).
No financial quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific, severe, and current supply-chain impediments justify a score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: While we have historically experienced some level of ordinary course turnover of employees, the COVID-19 pandemic and resulting impacts have exacerbated labor shortages and increased employee turnover.

components.reason: Attributes worsening labor shortages directly to COVID-19.
Confirms actual experience (not hypothetical).
No quantitative magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows realised HR strain; moderately severe but unquantified, yielding score 3.

evidence_list.snippet: It is also uncertain to what extent any COVID-19 vaccine mandates, if imposed or implemented, may result in further workforce attrition.

components.reason: Highlights new, policy-driven risk of attrition tied to COVID-19.
Uncertainty without evidence of magnitude reduces clarity.
Potential future operational impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emerging but speculative workforce risk scores low due to uncertainty and lack of detail.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, to the extent our management is focused on mitigating the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic which has required, and will continue to require, a large investment of time and resources, our attention and resources may be diverted from other business matters.

components.reason: Identifies management distraction and resource drain.
States requirement is ongoing (‘will continue to require’).
No quantitative estimate of cost or diversion.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Indirect but concrete governance impact—modest severity at 2.

evidence_list.snippet: The continued spread of COVID-19 may have further adverse impacts on our business, operations, customer demand, supply chain, cash flow generation, financial position and liquidity and may also exacerbate other risks and uncertainties described in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

components.reason: Enumerates wide spectrum of potential adverse effects.
Future-looking risk tied to ongoing spread.
Absence of quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad but high-level warning without specifics merits a score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: However, especially in the second half of the year, we also experienced an acceleration of several macroeconomic challenges that have negatively impacted our ability to meet this robust demand, such as supply chain disruptions and delays; shortages in materials, including reductions in allocations of electronic components and other parts from key suppliers; labor shortages and elevated levels of employee absenteeism due to the on-going COVID-19 pandemic; and increased commodity, material component, packaging, freight and labor inflation.

components.reason: Describes realised negative impacts during 2021.
Details specific pandemic-linked obstacles (component shortages, absenteeism).
Explicit temporal proximity (‘second half of the year’) shows recency.
Lacks monetary quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recent, concrete performance drag driven by COVID-19 supply and labour issues earns a solid 5.
